cases.customer_question: Can a product that uses a qualified Controller Subsystem and a separately qualified Bluetooth stack be qualified by combining the existing registrations without additional testing, even when the stack qualification also contains controller layers such as RF PHY and LL?
question_variants: Can I combine a Controller Subsystem QDID with a stack Component DID?
Will combining a controller qualification and a stack qualification require new testing?
What happens when both referenced designs contain RF PHY and LL layers?
Can overlapping controller layers be ignored during qualification?
Can an End Product be registered using existing controller and stack qualifications only?
cases.actual_issue: The product combines a qualified controller design with a qualified stack design that includes overlapping lower Bluetooth layers. The qualification challenge is determining whether the overlap creates additional qualification obligations under the newer Qualification Workspace and QPRDv3 process.
cases.plain_english_explanation: A company wanted to reuse an already qualified controller and an already qualified Bluetooth stack. The problem was that the stack qualification also contained some of the same low-level Bluetooth layers already present in the controller qualification. The key question was whether referencing both would trigger unnecessary qualification complexity or testing.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant compared the referenced designs and determined that the lower-layer RF PHY and LL coverage was effectively equivalent. Because the stack-related design already provided the necessary functionality, referencing both designs created unnecessary overlap. Earlier guidance under older qualification assumptions treated overlapping layers as removable during design construction, but under the newer Qualification Workspace process the interaction between included layers, consistency checks, and generated test plans had to be considered. The recommended approach was to use the stack-related design reference alone when it provided the required functionality, thereby avoiding unnecessary qualification complexity.
cases.decision_logic: If multiple referenced Bluetooth designs provide equivalent lower-layer functionality, adding both designs does not add qualification value but can increase qualification complexity. The preferred qualification path is the minimum valid design set that satisfies the required Bluetooth functionality while avoiding overlapping layer combinations that may affect consistency checks or generated test plans.
cases.final_recommendation: Use the single stack-related qualified design reference when it already provides the required controller and host-layer coverage, rather than combining it with a separate controller qualification that duplicates the same lower layers.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Combining overlapping qualified designs unnecessarily can lead to more complex Qualification Workspace processing, potential additional test-plan generation, additional review effort, qualification delays, and avoidable testing obligations.
